subject: Request: Reclassify partial-degrade window vs third-party outage - CloudNav
messages:
From: Amit Shah <amit@cloudnav.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.ai>
Cc: support@cloudnav.com
Date: Wed, 1 Dec 2027 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Partial degradation on Dec 1 — classification as third-party?

Hi Naomi,

We observed a persistent 20–35% error-rate and 400–600ms latency increase on requests to the /v1/generate endpoint between 08:55–09:45 PST on Dec 1. Your status page lists a scheduled maintenance in a downstream routing provider during that window, but our telemetry shows the failure path is consistent with an upstream CDN flap that CloudNav controls.

Because this impacts our SLA calculation for December, we need Redwood to either: 1) confirm the event is classified as a Redwood maintenance exclusion, or 2) reclassify it as a third-party outage (CloudNav) so the uptime ledger reflects the correct split.

Attached: probe-log-20271201.csv with our synthetic probe timestamps and a trimmed tcpdump. We also included the notice we received from the routing provider (archived-maint-notice.pdf).

Can you confirm what telemetry Redwood used to attribute this window and whether you can re-open the apportionment?

Thanks,
Amit Shah
Head of Platform Reliability, CloudNav Systems
Attachment: probe-log-20271201.csv (csv, ~1.2MB)
Attachment: archived-maint-notice.pdf (pdf)

From: Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.ai>
To: Amit Shah <amit@cloudnav.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 1 Dec 2027 10:08:23 -0800
Subject: Re: Partial degradation on Dec 1 — classification as third-party?

Hi Amit — thanks for the detailed packet. I'm escalating this internally and looping in Ben (account) and Marissa (SRE). Preliminary read: our incident logs show a short-lived kernel-level packet drop in one of our egress routers at 08:52 that could explain the error spike, but we also see correlation with the routing provider's maintenance banner at 08:50.

Next steps from us:
- Marissa: will pull the full KV cache/timestamps and our probe fanout to determine overlap.
- Ben: will coordinate with your ops team on a joint timeline so both sides agree on probe windows.
- I will open a formal SLA dispute record and attach both sides' artifacts.

I'll come back with a proposed apportionment by EOD Friday (Dec 3).

Best,
Naomi
Enterprise Account Lead — Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 2 Dec 2027 08:37:11 -0800
Subject: Re: Partial degradation on Dec 1 — classification as third-party?

Naomi / Ben — I dug into the SRE telemetry and here's what I have:

Summary of findings (high-level):
- Service-level probe fanout shows error-rate spike from 08:50:13–09:02:46 PST.
- Host-level network telemetry indicates increased retransmits on egress interface rx3 starting 08:51:40; retransmit patterns are localized to a subset of pop-ids (us-west-2a, us-west-2b).
- Routing provider maintenance window started at 08:50:00 but their NOC shows maintenance on the provider control plane, not edge CDN caches.
- There is evidence of TCP resets returned from an intermediate ASN that matches the provider cited by CloudNav, but also short-lived ARP flaps on our egress cluster at 08:52:20.

Interpretation options:
1) Classify entire window (08:50–09:03) as Redwood-maintenance-affecting traffic: that would put the burden on Redwood and likely trigger a credit per the SLA.
2) Split window attribution: assign 70% of the window to the routing provider (third-party), 30% to our egress transient. This mirrors the packet-level distribution of failures and keeps the ledger proportional to impact.
3) If CloudNav provides additional probe evidence showing consistent fail path terminating at their edge, we can move to a 100% third-party classification.

Attachments to my analysis: sre-timeline-20271205.txt (stripped timeline), and a short list of request-ids for cross-check.

Recommendation: Propose splitting the window (option 2) and schedule a 30-minute joint-ops call to review pcap slices and request-ids. If CloudNav sends additional traces that clearly tie failures to their edge, we'll reclassify fully.

-Marissa
Principal SRE — Redwood Inference
Attachment: sre-timeline-20271205.txt (text)

From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>
To: Amit Shah <amit@cloudnav.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 3 Dec 2027 11:25:52 -0800
Subject: Re: Partial degradation on Dec 1 — classification as third-party?

Amit — thanks for the quick response yesterday. We're proposing the following operational path so this doesn't drag into the month-close:

1) Agreement in principle to a split apportionment (70/30 Redwood/third-party as Marissa suggested) for the Dec 1 window pending the joint review.
2) Schedule a 30-minute joint-ops call for Mon Dec 6 at 10:00 PST to walk pcap/request-id slices. Can you confirm availability?
3) We'll generate a draft ledger adjustment for Dec (affects SLA calculation and potential credit). If CloudNav provides hard trace evidence during the call, we'll update to 100% third-party and reverse the draft credit.

If that works, Naomi and I will prepare the ledger change and Monica will document the formal dispute request.

Regards,
Ben Carter
Enterprise Account Executive — Redwood Inference

From: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.ai>
To: Amit Shah <amit@cloudnav.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 12 Dec 2027 14:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Partial degradation on Dec 1 — classification as third-party?

Hi all — following up after the joint-ops on Dec 6 (thanks everyone who joined). To close the formal dispute:

- Outcome from joint review: packet traces show mixed responsibility. Our working ledger adjustment will apportion 65% to the routing provider and 35% to Redwood for the Dec 1 08:50–09:03 window. This reflects the fine-grained timing where our ARP flaps align with a subset of failed requests.
- Action items:
  * Naomi: please authorize the ledger update so it reflects on CloudNav's Dec SLA report.
  * Ben: coordinate a short confirmation note for Amit confirming the adjustment and the process for future disputes.
  * Marissa: preserve the raw pcaps and timeline in the shared drive folder (link below) for audit.
  * Amit / CloudNav: if you have additional proof tying the fail path exclusively to your CDN edge, supply within 10 business days and we will re-evaluate and adjust the ledger accordingly.

Link to artifacts: https://drive.redwood.ai/teams/sre/uptime-disputes/CloudNav-DN-4712

Regards,
Monica Patel
Senior Counsel — Redwood Inference
Attachment: decision-summary-CloudNav-Dec1.pdf (stub)
